content.description: NexusDefend adopts ARR-3-11 version 4.2 for the production Customer Agent build and release pipeline. The adoption covers artifact signing, provenance generation, immutable storage, and distribution integrity validation.
content.name: Adoption of ARR-3-11 Secure Software Artifact Supply Chain

content.description: External control specification defining requirements for securing the software artifact supply chain. Covers build integrity, artifact signing, provenance generation, storage immutability, and distribution controls.
content.name: Secure Software Artifact Supply Chain

requirements.text: Production artifacts SHALL be produced by an approved, uniquely identifiable build identity.
requirements.title: Approved Build Identity

requirements.text: Every production artifact SHALL be cryptographically signed using an organization-approved signing method before publication.
requirements.title: Cryptographic Artifact Signing

requirements.text: Every production artifact SHALL be accompanied by a verifiable provenance attestation linking the artifact to its source commit, build identity, and build parameters.
requirements.title: Provenance Generation

requirements.text: Published production artifacts SHALL be stored in immutable, access-controlled storage with versioning and integrity protection.
requirements.title: Immutable Artifact Storage

requirements.text: Artifact integrity and provenance SHALL be validated before distribution to external consumers.
requirements.title: Distribution Integrity Validation

requirements.text: Build processes SHALL be defined as code and SHALL be reproducible from source.
requirements.title: Build Parameter Reproducibility

compensating_controls: Elevated audit logging during emergency deployment

The path still requires manual signing by a member of the platform-security team and post-deployment provenance reconciliation.

content.description: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union. Applicable to NexusDefend as a provider of managed security services to EU-based essential and important entities.
content.name: NIS2 Directive

content.detailed_analysis:
NexusDefend distributes executable software directly into customer-managed enterprise environments. A compromised release artifact would bypass customer perimeter defenses because the Customer Agent runs with elevated privileges for endpoint management. The blast radius of a single compromised release could span hundreds of enterprise customers and tens of thousands of endpoints. Impact dimensions include:
- Customer harm: unauthorized code execution within customer networks - Contractual exposure: breach of customer agreements and SLAs - Incident response costs: emergency revocation and redeployment - Reputational damage: loss of trust in the security vendor itself - Regulatory notification: potential breach notification obligations
  across multiple jurisdictions
content.name: Compromise of customer-distributed software
content.summary: A compromised production release of the Customer Agent could result in unauthorized code executing within customer-managed enterprise environments.

content.description: Implementation of the ARR-3-11 artifact supply chain controls through a GitHub Actions release pipeline with Sigstore-based artifact signing, provenance attestation generation, and automated integrity validation before CloudFront distribution.

mechanisms.description: Only the GitHub Actions bot identity for the nexusdefend/customer-agent repository is authorized to produce production artifacts.
Before a new artifact is served via CloudFront, its provenance attestation is independently validated. Artifacts failing validation are blocked from distribution.
Production artifacts are stored in the prod-release-artifacts S3 bucket with versioning enabled, block-public-access enforced, and KMS server-side encryption.
The release pipeline is defined in .github/workflows/release.yml within the customer-agent repository and is subject to code review.
A Sigstore provenance attestation is generated for every build, linking the artifact digest to the source commit, build workflow, and build parameters.
Every production artifact is signed using Sigstore keyless signing with the GitHub Actions OIDC identity. Signatures are recorded in the public Rekor transparency log.

content.name: Signed Release Pipeline

content.name: NIS2 Article 21 — Supply Chain Security

FAILURE: Artifact submitted without valid provenance attestation. No Sigstore signature found. Build identity could not be verified. Artifact blocked from distribution.
Root cause: A developer attempted to manually upload a locally-built artifact to the production S3 bucket for testing purposes. The artifact lacked a CI-produced provenance attestation. The validation gate correctly identified the violation and prevented distribution.
Related incident: INC-2026-041 was opened to review the attempted manual upload and reinforce the approved release process.
